intro: A Chao Phraya dinner cruise is Bangkok's classic evening out — enjoy a buffet on the water as illuminated landmarks glide past: Wat Arun, the Grand Palace, Rama VIII Bridge, and ICONSIAM. This guide compares the most popular boats, breaks down prices, buffets, and boarding piers, and points you to advance booking on Klook.
quickAnswerHtml: Chao Phraya dinner cruises are mostly Thai + international buffets lasting ~2 hours, departing in the evening (~19:30) past lit-up landmarks including Wat Arun, the Grand Palace, Rama VIII Bridge, and ICONSIAM. Most boats have live music or a show. Popular options include Chao Phraya Princess, White Orchid, and Wonderful Pearl, priced around 900–1,600 THB per person. Boarding piers are at ICONSIAM, Asiatique, and River City. Book in advance — window seats and rooftop decks fill up fast.

blocks.html: The appeal of a dinner cruise is seeing Bangkok at its best — the river at night, landmarks lit up and reflected on the water, while you eat and listen to live music. It works for couples, families, and celebrations alike. What varies between boats is buffet quality, boat size / open-air deck, and the show on board.

blocks.text: How to Pick the Right Boat

items: Want the full view → choose a window seat or an open-air rooftop deck — book early
Large group / family → go for a bigger boat with a broad buffet spread and a show
Romantic evening / special occasion → look for a boat that prioritises atmosphere and a premium menu
On a budget → a standard buffet boat still passes every landmark — the views are the same
Allow 30–45 minutes to check in before departure

blocks.html: Most boats depart in the evening, around 19:30–20:00, for a roughly 2-hour cruise. The main boarding piers are ICONSIAM, Asiatique, and River City, all easily reached by BTS with a free shuttle boat or by taxi. Allow 30–45 minutes to check in before your boat leaves, and let them know at booking if you want a riverside seat or have any dietary requirements.

blocks.title: Get the Most From Your Cruise

items.title: Book a Window or Deck Seat
items.text: The best views are at the window or on the open-air deck — these sell out fast. Book online in advance and specify your preferred zone.

items.title: Arrive Early
items.text: Check in 30–45 minutes before departure, especially during high season and public holidays, so you don't miss your sailing.

items.title: Get to the Pier via BTS + Shuttle Boat
items.text: ICONSIAM and Asiatique both run free shuttle boats from Saphan Taksin pier (BTS Saphan Taksin) — convenient and avoids traffic.

items.title: Deck Seats Get Windy
items.text: Open-air deck views are spectacular but the wind picks up — bring a light jacket and hold on to anything that could blow away when you take photos.

faq.q: Which Chao Phraya dinner cruise is best?
faq.a: Popular picks include Chao Phraya Princess, White Orchid, and newer 3-deck vessels. Every boat passes the same illuminated riverfront landmarks — the difference is buffet quality, boat size and deck space, and what show is on board. Choose based on what matters most to you.

faq.q: How much does it cost, and what's included?
faq.a: Prices run roughly 900–1,600 THB per person, usually including a Thai + international buffet for ~2 hours and live music or a show. Alcoholic drinks are typically charged separately. Check the exact menu and what's included when booking.
The main piers are ICONSIAM, Asiatique, and River City. Most have a free shuttle boat from Saphan Taksin pier (BTS Saphan Taksin). Check the boarding point for your specific package when you book.

faq.q: What time does the boat depart, and how long does it last?
faq.a: Most cruises depart in the evening around 19:30–20:00 and last about 2 hours. Aim to check in 30–45 minutes before departure.

faq.q: Which landmarks can you see from the boat?
faq.a: The route passes iconic riverfront landmarks lit up at night, including Wat Arun, the Grand Palace, Rama VIII Bridge, and ICONSIAM — making it one of the best vantage points for seeing Bangkok after dark.
